seoTitle: UK Student Accommodation: Compare Halls, Private Rentals and Homestays
title: UK Student Accommodation: Compare Halls, Private Rentals and Homestays
content:
Compare accommodation by the whole contract, not just the weekly rent. Look at bills, deposits, guarantor requirements, travel time and the dates you will need the room.

Compare the whole contract

A room's weekly price is only one part of the cost. Check the contract length, included bills, deposit, payment schedule and cancellation conditions. For research students, a short teaching-year contract may leave a gap when you still need to be near the university.

University halls

Halls can simplify moving because the university provides a defined application process and accommodation information. Check eligibility for postgraduate students, room types and the actual location. A place is not guaranteed unless the university's terms say it is, and some rooms may have shared facilities or restrictions relevant to your needs.

Private student accommodation

Purpose-built student housing often offers a clear room package, but compare charges and contract dates carefully. Ask about the guarantor, payment requirements and what happens if your visa or admission arrangements change. An attractive photograph is not evidence that the room suits your budget or travel needs.

Private rentals and shared housing

Check who manages the property, which costs are included and what documents you must provide. Consider transport, working space and noise alongside price. Read the agreement and use the university's accommodation team or a reputable advice service if terms are unclear.

Homestays

A homestay may offer a different living environment, but arrangements vary. Ask about meals, access to facilities, house rules, guests, study space and distance from campus. Confirm the payment and cancellation terms before treating it as a flexible short-term option.

Before paying

Verify the property and the person or organisation offering it. Keep written records and follow the university's advice on avoiding accommodation fraud. Budget for any deposit and the cost of temporary housing while you search.

Use current local prices rather than a generic forecast for a future year. Make a shortlist showing total contract cost and the practical trade-offs; that gives you a clearer decision than comparing headline weekly rent alone.

Official information

  • UKCISA: student accommodation information
  • GOV.UK: private renting

Read the contract dates before the room photos

Check when the tenancy begins and ends, whether bills are included and what happens if your arrival is delayed. Ask about deposits, guarantors and cancellation terms before paying. For research students, a short teaching-term contract may not cover the period you need to work on campus. Compare the commute and access to a quiet workspace as well as price. If you cannot inspect the property yourself, use the university’s accommodation advice and verification process. Attractive photos are not evidence that an advert or payment request is genuine.

Relevant listings and guides on NextApply

To see how these questions apply to a real listing, review EPSRC CDT in Chemical Synthesis for a Healthy Planet (CSHP CDT) at University of Oxford and University of York. Compare its stated requirements with your own preparation and check the official source before applying.
